rule.name: Insecure Permissions
rule.rule_desc: The code or deployment configuration requests privileges or grants access beyond an explicitly resolved minimum. Determine the effective permissions and the operation’s requirements.
rule.vuln_desc: A compromised actor may access additional data, modify protected resources, or extend compromise beyond the intended application boundary when excessive privileges remain available.
rule.developer: Run with the least privileges required, remove unnecessary grants, and scope each permission to its intended resource and operation. Verify effective inherited permissions and test denied access.
rule.reviewer: Verify that the AndroidManifest.xml file requests only the permissions necessary for the application's functionality. Ensure that unnecessary or overly broad permissions are not granted, as they can pose security risks. rule.rule_desc: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
rule.vuln_desc: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.

rule.rule_desc: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
rule.vuln_desc: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.

rule.name: Root Detection via Build Tags Only
rule.rule_desc: The application checks mutable device properties as an environment-integrity signal.

rule.developer: Treat device-property checks as supplementary risk signals. Enforce authorization independently, and use platform-backed integrity evidence with server-side verification when the operation requires it.
rule.reviewer: Assess root detection coverage by cataloguing all detection signals. Single-signal checks should be flagged. Verify that detection runs at runtime beyond the initial launch check.
